name: ancestor-walk
__comment: HAND-AUTHORED. Not npm output, deliberately: npm's hoisting works to avoid
exactly this shape, so it cannot be produced on demand by running an install.
The subject under test is the resolution walk over a key set, not npm's
hoisting policy, and real npm trees do reach this shape.
It encodes an INTERMEDIATE ANCESTOR hit. The package at
node_modules/a/node_modules/b depends on c. Two c's exist: c@2.0.0 beside it
under a, and c@1.0.0 hoisted at the root. b has no c of its own.
A correct ancestor walk stops at node_modules/a/node_modules/c (2.0.0).
A walk shortened to 'my own node_modules, else the root' skips the
intermediate level and returns node_modules/c (1.0.0) — a wrong answer no
single-level fixture can expose, since there every hit is at depth 0 or 1.
